sections.h2: Where is the Jones County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is at 101 Market Street in Trenton, with a mailing address of PO Box 189, Trenton, NC 28585, and the phone number is 252-448-2551. Monday through Thursday it opens from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and stops accepting documents for recording at 4:30 p.m. On Fridays it is open 8 a.m. to noon, and the recording cutoff is 11:30 a.m.

That short Friday matters for a closing. A deed that reaches the counter after 11:30 on a Friday is not recorded until the next open day, which is Monday, so sellers in Jones County usually schedule signing early in the week.

The office describes its job as recording and keeping births, deaths, marriages, service discharges, notaries, assumed names, maps and real estate transactions. Its real estate indexes reach back to the late 1700s, and a search for records before 1978 has its own page on the county site.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Jones County?
sections.html:
A deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages with $4.00 for each additional page, according to the county's fee schedule dated October 1, 2016. A deed of trust is $64.00 for the first 35 pages.

Jones County Register of Deeds real estate fees from the county schedule dated October 1, 2016
ItemFee
Deed of trust, first 35 pages$64.00, then $4.00 each added page
All other instruments, first 15 pages$26.00, then $4.00 each added page

Uncertified copy$0.25

The same schedule lists the excise tax as $2.00 per $1,000 of purchase price. The register's own information page states it as $1.00 per $500 of consideration, which is the same rate.

sections.h2: Does Jones County require tax office approval before a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's page says every deed, together with a completed Tax Certification Form, must be presented to the Tax Office for approval before the document can be recorded. The form is also called the Tax Data Sheet or Tax Collection Form, and the register's site links to it.

Two more local rules sit alongside that step:

  • Under a Jones County ordinance, every deed must show the tax parcel ID number on its first page.
  • A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for real property that is subject to delinquent taxes.

So an unpaid Jones County tax bill can stop a deed at the counter. A seller with back taxes should plan to pay them at or before closing, using the closing agent to settle the bill so the deed is accepted the same day.

sections.h2: Which recording standards apply to a Jones County deed?
sections.html:
Any document recorded on or after July 1, 2002 has to follow the layout rules in G.S. 161-14(b), and the Jones County register lists them on its site. A document that falls short triggers the $25.00 nonstandard document fee in addition to the usual recording fee.

  • Paper size of 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14.
  • A 3 inch blank margin at the top of page one and 1/2 inch on the other sides, and on all sides of later pages.
  • Black type on white paper, no smaller than 10 points.
  • Printing on one side only.
  • The type of instrument shown at the top of page one under the margin, and the preparer's name on the first page.

The register may waive the nonstandard fee if the print is smaller than 10 point but still legible once scanned. Maps and plats follow separate rules: they must be 18 by 24 inches, with one mylar and one paper copy, and a Jones County review officer must approve the map before it is recorded.

sections.h2: How do liens and satisfactions work in Jones County?
sections.html:
An old mortgage is cleared by recording a satisfaction, and the Jones County register charges nothing for it. Two kinds exist: a Satisfaction of Security Instrument signed by the secured creditor, and a Trustee's Satisfaction signed by a trustee or substitute trustee. The county notes that satisfaction by presentation ended October 1, 2011.

Wills are not recorded at the register. They go to the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, which a seller handling an inherited house should know before heading to the wrong counter.

North Carolina ties a tax lien to the parcel as of the January 1 listing date, and the lien carries penalties, interest and costs. Enforcement of an unpaid lien is a foreclosure action filed in the county where the land lies. Ask the Jones County tax office for a current payoff before you sign a sales contract.

sections.h2: What do I need to know about Jones County property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Jones County taxes are due September 1, and they are treated as delinquent on January 6, when interest of 2 percent for January applies, then 3/4 percent each month after. A mailed payment counts by its U.S. Postal postmark, and a postage meter date is not accepted.

The county's last revaluation was effective January 1, 2022, and the next is scheduled for January 1, 2030. Market changes between those dates are not counted. A seller who disagrees with an assessment can call 252-448-2546 to set up an informal appeal before March 1, and later appeals may need a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review.

The tax office is at 418 Hwy 58 N in Trenton, open Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Friday 8 a.m. to noon. Partial payments are taken at the Tax Collections Office, and a payment plan is available only if no enforced collection action has begun. Agricultural and forest tracts can qualify for use value taxation, and a new application goes to the assessor in the regular January listing period.

sections.h2: What does the Jones County housing market look like?
sections.html:
Jones County is small and rural. The Census Bureau estimates 9,575 residents for July 1, 2025, down from 10,153 at the 2010 census, and it counts 4,804 housing units across 471.37 square miles. That works out to a density of 19.5 people per square mile in 2020.

For 2020 to 2024, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $130,300 and 79.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $747 and the median household income is $59,641. People aged 65 and over make up 26.8 percent of the population, so many Jones County sales involve an older owner or an estate.

Construction is slow, with 46 building permits shown for 2025. Fewer new homes on the market means a Jones County seller competes mostly with other resales, and a house that needs repairs can sit for a long time.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work with the Jones County records process?
sections.html:
A cash sale uses the same recording path as any other. The deed gets tax office approval, the parcel number goes on page one, the excise stamp is paid by the seller, and the register records it before the Friday or weekday cutoff.

Where it differs is speed and condition. A buyer paying cash does not wait on a lender appraisal, and the house is bought as it stands, which suits owners with liens, vacant property, tenants or an estate to settle. Delinquent taxes still have to be paid at closing for the deed to be accepted in Jones County.

faqs.q: What are the Jones County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with recording accepted until 4:30 p.m. On Fridays the office is open 8 a.m. to noon and the recording cutoff is 11:30 a.m. The phone number is 252-448-2551.

faqs.q: Can Jones County record a deed if property taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: No. A resolution under G.S. 161-31, effective September 1, 2007, bars the register from accepting a deed for property subject to delinquent taxes. Pay the bill first, then present the deed.

faqs.q: What goes on the first page of a Jones County deed?
faqs.a: The tax parcel ID number, as required by a county ordinance, plus the type of instrument and the preparer's name. A 3 inch top margin and 1/2 inch side margins also apply.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction in Jones County?
faqs.a: No. The county fee schedule lists a satisfaction of a deed of trust as no charge, whether it is signed by the secured creditor or by a trustee.

faqs.q: Where are wills recorded in Jones County?
faqs.a: At the Jones County Clerk of Court in Trenton, phone 252-448-6220, not at the Register of Deeds. The register records the deeds that follow.
